examples.name: overview
examples.title: Sixty seconds
examples.description: First contact: a positive contract discharged at the call site. The smallest end-to-end proof.

examples.name: abs
examples.title: Branches become facts
examples.description: A conditional contributes its test to the then-branch and the negation to the else-branch, so both paths meet a nonnegativity annotation.

examples.name: guard
examples.title: Guarding a refined call
examples.description: A refined precondition discharged from an enclosing if-guard; the unguarded branch requires nothing.

examples.name: binder
examples.title: Let-binder facts
examples.description: A refined let-binding is recorded as a fact and discharges a downstream obligation.

examples.name: recursion
examples.title: Recursion by induction
examples.description: A recursive call's refined result serves as the induction hypothesis; fib and a triangular sum both prove nonnegative.

examples.name: bst
examples.title: Binary search tree (verified behind an interface)
examples.description: A genuine recursive BST, an abstract interface with membership-algebra proof tokens, and a positive client that proves four facts from the interface alone. Opens on Lean; z3 and oxsmt verify the interface/client layer but currently report a known recursive-datatype solver gap in bst.ml.

workspace.known_gap: Recursive-datatype implementation VCs are Lean-only today; z3/oxsmt solver-error is a backend capability gap, not a source failure.

examples.name: dependent
examples.title: Dependent contracts
examples.description: A parameter's refinement mentions an earlier parameter; the call-site obligation instantiates it.

examples.name: counterexample
examples.title: When you're wrong
examples.description: A false obligation (2 = 1): verification fails and the obligation is reported disproved. The one example that does NOT verify.

examples.name: proof_tour
examples.title: Proof-pane tour
examples.description: One automatic round produces a proved and a disproved obligation, driving the cursor-following proof pane, per-VC underlines, and solver-detail and generated-Lean views. Discharge stops at the first disproved obligation, so this buffer does not verify.

examples.name: unproved
examples.title: When automation gives up
examples.description: A real unproved obligation: automation found no proof and no refutation, so the goal may still hold.
